extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers in algebraic geometry (readers of Vakil's Foundations of Algebraic Geometry)
extracted.subtask_description: An index / glossary chunk from a graduate-level algebraic geometry textbook listing topics and short notes about definitions, properties, and standard criteria for many objects (e.g., effective Cartier divisors, étale morphisms, flatness, finite morphisms, elliptic curves, etc.). Useful as a quick-reference pointer to properties and standard results.

rubrics_metrics.name: effective Cartier divisors — basic properties
rubrics_metrics.description: effective Cartier divisors: have pure codimension 1; normal bundles to; relative; restriction to open sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index notes the usual properties one checks for effective Cartier divisors: pure codimension 1 (so locally principal), behavior of normal bundles, relative versions, and how they restrict to open sets.

rubrics_metrics.name: elliptic curves — distinguishing properties
rubrics_metrics.description: elliptic curves: are group varieties; counterexamples and pathologies; degenerate; degree 1 points = degree 0 line bundles; group law; level n structure; non-torsion point; not same as genus 1 curves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists common facts and pitfalls: elliptic curves are smooth projective genus 1 curves with a chosen point (hence group structure), but genus 1 curves without a rational point are not elliptic curves; includes topics like level structure and torsion/non-torsion points.

rubrics_metrics.name: étale morphisms — properties and cautions
rubrics_metrics.description: étale morphisms: closed under composition; differential geometric motivation; form a “reasonable” class; not same as 'local isomorphism'; open condition; étale-locally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pointers to typical properties to verify for an étale map: stability under composition, local (open) nature, geometric intuition, and the important caution that 'étale' is not literally the same as 'local isomorphism' in the scheme sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: enough injectives / projectives (in categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: enough injectives; enough projectives: statements about existence of enough injectives (references to sections) and enough projectives in module categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index indicates where the text treats existence of injective/projective objects (used for derived functors/Ext/Tor computations).

rubrics_metrics.name: effective cone / nef cone / line bundle numerics
rubrics_metrics.description: effective cone; nef cone: references to cones of divisors/line bundles and numerical properties (nef, numerically trivial, nef cone, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index points to standard numerical invariants and cones in the theory of divisors and line bundles (useful for ampleness/nefness criteria and intersection computations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ext functors — properties and computation
rubrics_metrics.description: Ext functors: composition of, first/second versions; for O-modules; computable by acyclics; long exact sequence; behaves like derived functor in first argument; needn’t preserve quasicoherence; two definitions are same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarizes how Ext is developed: various constructions coincide, long exact sequences exist, practical computation via acyclic resolutions, and subtlety that Ext may not preserve quasicoherence in general.

rubrics_metrics.name: field extensions — common classifications
rubrics_metrics.description: field extension: finite; algebraic; finitely generated; Galois; inseparable; normal; purely inseparable; purely transcendental; separable; separably generated; finitely generated related to transcendence degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index lists the usual types of field extensions and where to find their properties and consequences (e.g., behavior of morphisms, separability issues, base change).

rubrics_metrics.name: finite morphisms — equivalent characterizations and properties
rubrics_metrics.description: finite morphisms = integral + finite type; = projective + affine; = projective + finite fibers; are affine, closed, integral; closed under composition; preserved by base change; may be projective/proper/separated; separable to Spec k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives the standard equivalent characterizations used to check whether a morphism is finite and lists permanence properties (composition, base change) and relationships to projective/proper/affine.

rubrics_metrics.name: finite type / finitely presented morphisms and modules
rubrics_metrics.description: finitely presented = finite type under Noetherian hypotheses; finiteness conditions for rings, modules, morphisms; afffine-local on source/target; preserved by base change; Chevalley’s theorem; local finite presentation notions and criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index highlights the different finiteness adjectives, their relationships, and where local criteria and base-change preservation appear (important when checking hypotheses in theorems).

rubrics_metrics.name: flatness — criteria and important consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: flatness: equals free/projective for finitely presented modules over local rings; equals locally free for finitely presented sheaves; infinitesimal criterion; local criterion; no higher Tor; preserved by base change; open condition in good situations; stalk/prime-local property; valuative criterion; variation of cohomology; constancy of Euler characteristic in families.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index collects many standard facts and tests for flatness used in practice: local/inﬁnitesimal criteria, Tor vanishing, base-change behavior, and consequences like constancy of Euler characteristic and fiber dimension behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: generic flatness / Generic Freeness
rubrics_metrics.description: generic flatness; Generic Freeness Lemma; generic freeness references and improved versions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Points to the results asserting flatness/generic freeness on a dense open after base change — used frequently when reducing to a 'generic' base.

rubrics_metrics.name: finitely presented sheaves — local freeness and related facts
rubrics_metrics.description: finitely presented quasicoherent sheaves: affine-local; constant rank implies locally free; flat = locally free for finitely presented sheaves; local freeness is stalk-local property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collects the typical facts used to check when a coherent/quasicoherent sheaf is locally free and how flatness interacts with finite presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: fibers / generic fiber / geometric fiber properties
rubrics_metrics.description: fibers: geometry of fibers (connectedness, dimension), geometric/generic fibers, properties preserved by base change, geometric fiber notions (geometrically reduced/irreducible/integral/connected).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index entries point to how various fiberwise properties are defined and checked, and how base change affects them — essential when studying families and moduli.

rubrics_metrics.name: function field — determination of curve
rubrics_metrics.description: function field: determines irreducible regular projective curve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard algebro-geometric fact: the function field of a curve determines its normalization/unique smooth projective model (used in classification of curves).

rubrics_metrics.name: flat limit / variation of cohomology
rubrics_metrics.description: flat limit; variation of cohomology; constancy of Euler characteristics in flat/projective families; semicontinuity and related theorems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to theorems (e.g., Grauert, cohomology and base change) describing how cohomology of fibers behaves in families and which invariants remain constant under flatness/projectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: global generation / base-point-freeness
rubrics_metrics.description: global generation (of quasicoherent sheaf): at a point; every quasicoherent sheaf on every affine scheme; finite; open condition; preserved by ⊗; relative/global generation with respect to a morphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists tests and permanence properties of global generation (important for constructing morphisms to projective space and checking ampleness/semiampleness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grothendieck coherence / finiteness theorems
rubrics_metrics.description: Grothendieck’s Coherence Theorem: references for coherence for projective morphisms and consequences in cohomology; Grothendieck’s Theorem and related spectral sequences (composition-of-functors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Index points to where coherence results and derived functor spectral sequences are stated and used (central to many finiteness/cohomology results).

rubrics_metrics.name: Jacobian criterion — uses and contexts
rubrics_metrics.description: Jacobian criterion: for smoothness; for projective hypersurfaces; description of Ω; Jacobian map/matrix in many contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates where the Jacobian criterion is applied to test smoothness of schemes and hypersurfaces and where the cotangent sheaf/Ω is described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noether normalization / geometric Noether normalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Noether normalization and geometric Noether normalization: references to standard dimensionality/normalization results and where they are used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Points to reduction steps often used to reduce problems to finite maps to affine space or to control dimensions.
